html:
SMTO-SLM-0001 — SMTO couldn't read the SLURM cluster's address settings

GUID: b76dd84d-6292-49a5-a724-aef793aa2df5
Slug: slurm-routing-invalid
Domain: SLM · Subsystem: slm

What happened

  • A cluster name, scheduler address or port in the cluster's settings file isn't in a form SMTO can read. Your SLURM command still runs, but SMTO won't remember this cluster for the conversation.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask the cluster's administrator to check the ClusterName line in slurm.conf on the Gateway computer: only letters, numbers, dashes or underscores, up to 40 characters. SMTO can only remember a cluster whose name is in that simple form.
  2. Ask them to check the SlurmctldHost lines: each scheduler computer listed once, no more than 16, written as a plain computer name or address. A repeated or oddly written scheduler entry means SMTO can't tell which cluster it is.
  3. Ask them to check that SlurmctldPort is a single port number or a low-to-high range, such as 6817 or 6817-6818. A port written another way can't be read safely.
  4. After a fix, ask the Agent to run sinfo on that Gateway. A successful simple SLURM read lets SMTO note the cluster again.

What success looks like

  • The Agent runs sinfo or squeue on that Gateway without this error, and later SLURM requests in the conversation use the same cluster.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages the SLURM cluster or SMTO. Don't let anyone change slurm.conf just to suit SMTO; it controls the whole cluster.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • SLURM configuration parsing rejected a routing value: an invalid ClusterName, a malformed, duplicate or excess (more than 16) SlurmctldHost, a malformed SlurmctldAddr, an invalid SlurmctldPort or range, or unsafe characters.

What this means

  • SLURM public/setup parsing rejects an invalid cluster name, unsafe routing value, duplicate/excessive controller identity, malformed host/address or unsupported port/range syntax. These checks describe local configuration identity and continuity eligibility. They do not query cluster health or prove command rollback; execution and optional observation evidence remain distinct.

Why this can happen

  • SLURM public/setup parsing rejects an invalid cluster name, unsafe routing value, duplicate/excessive controller identity, malformed host/address or unsupported port/range syntax.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the exact cluster/controller/port field against the authoritative configuration.

How to fix it

  • On the Gateway host, inspect the slurm.conf in SLURM_CONF or /etc/slurm/slurm.conf and its includes: ClusterName (compared case-insensitively) must be 1-40 characters of letters, digits, '_' or '-', starting with a letter or digit, each SlurmctldHost must be a distinct host or host(addr) (at most 16), SlurmctldAddr a plain host, and SlurmctldPort a port or ascending low-high range within 1-65535. Correct the real configuration deliberately; this check queries no scheduler and does not affect the command's own outcome.
  • Correct the intended cluster name, controller addresses and ports in the authoritative SLURM configuration. Verify the route before submitting work.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • A supported route yields the intended cluster identity without changing cluster state.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • These checks describe local configuration identity and continuity eligibility. They do not query cluster health or prove command rollback; execution and optional observation evidence remain distinct.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
